definitions.explanation: A style of writing based on the grammar of classical Japanese, used for official documents, laws, and much literature until the mid-twentieth century. Contrasts with {口語体|こうごたい}, the modern colloquial style used today.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{詩|し}→詩：02139_shi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{文語体|ぶんごたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}かれている→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: This poem is written in the literary style.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明治|めいじ}→明治：19860_meiji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{法律|ほうりつ}→法律：01722_houritsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{文語体|ぶんごたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{読|よ}み→読む：00426_yomu⟧にくい。
examples.english: Meiji-era laws are written in classical style and are hard to read.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦後|せんご}→戦後：12853_sengo⟧、⟦{公文書|こうぶんしょ}→公文書：11677_koubunsho⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{文語体|ぶんごたい}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{口語体|こうごたい}→口語体：24859_kougotai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{改|あらた}められた→改める：12923_aratameru⟧。
examples.english: After the war, official documents were changed from the classical style to the colloquial style.

notes:
From ⟦{文語|ぶんご}→文語：12991_bungo⟧ (written, classical language) + ⟦{体|たい}→体：09872_tai⟧ (style).

USAGE:
You meet it in older poetry, tanka and haiku, the Imperial Rescript on Education, and prewar laws. Marks of the style include けり, ⟦なり→なる：01970_naru⟧, and ず in place of modern forms.
